## 13.1 What is a test environment?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A test environment has a build, devices, tools, a test plan and bug reports.
- Every result names the build, the device and the OS version.
- Then somebody else can repeat the test.
- **Do it:** Write the build, the device, the OS version and two tests for a game on your phone.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/test-environment.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · The parts

a) Which part of the test environment is "PocketQuest_1.3, build 42"?
b) Which part says which test runs on which device?
c) Why must a result name the device and the OS version?

::: {.answer}
a) the build
b) the test plan
c) so that others can repeat the test
:::

## 13.2 Emulators and simulators

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- An emulator copies a device, and the real app runs on the computer.
- An AVD is a device profile plus a system image with one Android version.
- The iOS Simulator runs only on a Mac.
- **Do it:** Create three AVDs in AVD Builder. What can each one not test?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/emulator-vs-real.png)
:::
::::

## Live demo · AVD Builder

{{< sim file="sims/avd-builder.html" poster="sims/avd-builder.png" title="AVD Builder: virtual devices for Pocket Quest" task="**Show:** create the P5 twin, the API 26 phone and the tablet. **Ask:** what can these AVDs not tell us about the P5?" >}}

## Example · The P5 twin

Rami wants to test Pocket Quest on a copy of the P5 and on Android 8.
**Which AVDs does Rami create?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The **P5 twin** has 720 × 1600, 4 GB and Android 11 (API 30).
2. The **oldest phone** has API 26, and a **tablet** has API 33.
3. The emulator needs **virtualization** in the BIOS to run fast.
:::

## Try it 2 · Emulators

a) What are the two parts of an AVD?
b) Which API level is Android 8?
c) Why does 60 fps in the emulator not mean 60 fps on the P5?

::: {.answer}
a) a device profile and a system image
b) API 26
c) The emulator runs on the much stronger computer.
:::

## 13.3 Real devices

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- On Android we tap the build number seven times and switch on USB debugging.
- An iPhone needs a Mac with Xcode, or TestFlight.
- A device farm rents real phones in the cloud.
- **Do it:** Find the build number and the USB debugging switch on an Android phone.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/real-device-setup.png)
:::
::::

## Example · The P5 on the cable

Rami connects the P5 and runs adb devices.
**What happens, and what does the real phone show?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The P5 is **unauthorized** until Rami taps "Allow" on the phone.
2. Then adb devices shows **device**, and Rami installs the build.
3. After 20 minutes the P5 is **hot** and its frame rate drops, which the emulator never showed.
:::

## 13.4 A device matrix

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The matrix covers the oldest and newest OS versions.
- It includes the weakest device and the main screen sizes.
- It covers both platforms, with real devices for speed, heat and sensors.
- **Do it:** Cover every row in Matrix Builder for $300 or less. What did you choose?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/device-matrix.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · Real devices and the matrix

a) adb devices shows "unauthorized". What must Rami do?
b) Which row of the matrix can only a real phone cover?
c) Why does the matrix need the weakest supported phone?

::: {.answer}

b) speed, heat and touch

## Try it 4 · The tests (harder)

The facts: Rami must test the menu on six screen sizes, the heat after a 20-minute race, the start on Android 8 and tilt steering with the gyroscope.

a) Where does Rami test the six screen sizes?
b) Where does Rami test the heat and the tilt steering?
c) Where does Rami test the start on Android 8 without an Android 8 phone?

::: {.answer}
a) on Android emulators
b) on a real phone
c) on an AVD with API 26
:::

## Summary

- A test environment has a build, devices, tools, a test plan and bug reports.
- Emulators and the iOS Simulator give many versions and sizes for free.
- Real devices show the speed, the heat, the battery and the sensors.
- Developer options and USB debugging prepare an Android phone.
- A device matrix covers versions, sizes, platforms and the weakest device.
